rate_cases.title: Dominion 2025 biennial review — GS-5 data-center rate class
rate_cases.next_milestone: GS-5 rate class takes effect for new 25 MW+ customers on January 1, 2027; SCC is separately weighing data-center transmission cost allocation
rate_cases.summary: The SCC's final order created a new GS-5 rate class for customers demanding 25 MW or more (effective January 1, 2027), requiring a minimum of 85% of contracted distribution and transmission demand and 60% of generation demand, 14-year agreements, and collateral — in the Commission's words, "to help insulate ratepayers from the costs around the rapid build-out and construction of infrastructure to support businesses such as data centers." The order granted $565.7M (2026) and $209.9M (2027) of Dominion's requested $822M / $345M base-rate increases at a 9.8% ROE.

rate_cases.title: Entergy Louisiana infrastructure for Meta's Richland Parish campus
rate_cases.next_milestone: LPSC response to the 2026 Earthjustice/UCS request to investigate the Meta financing arrangement's stranded-asset risk
rate_cases.summary: The LPSC approved Entergy Louisiana's plan to build three combined-cycle gas plants (two in Richland Parish online late 2028, one at Waterford by end of 2029) plus transmission, and to procure up to 1,500 MW of solar through expedited certification, to serve Meta's Richland Parish data center. Entergy states that "Meta is paying its share of the costs for the infrastructure needed to support its operations, ensuring that other customers are protected from those expenses." In 2026, Earthjustice and the Union of Concerned Scientists asked the LPSC to investigate whether the financing arrangement could leave households exposed to stranded costs.

rate_cases.title: Georgia Power base-rate freeze through 2028
rate_cases.next_milestone: Storm-cost recovery handled in a separate proceeding; large-load growth scrutiny continues in the 2026 IRP round
rate_cases.summary: The Georgia PSC approved a stipulation freezing Georgia Power base rates through at least 2028 — filed under docket 44280, the 2022 rate-case docket the stipulation extends — with storm costs moved to a separate proceeding. Georgia Power frames the freeze as "balancing the mutual benefits of extraordinary economic growth among all stakeholders"; consumer and environmental intervenors argued the plan leans on projected data-center revenue that may not materialize.

rate_cases.title: Ameren Missouri Large Load Customer rate plan
rate_cases.summary: The PSC approved a non-unanimous global stipulation (filed November 20, 2025; Public Counsel not a signatory) creating a Large Load Customer Service rate for new customers at or above 75 MW of monthly demand — the class that covers the Warrenton and Montgomery County data-center projects. Filed under Senate Bill 4's large-load provisions (Section 393.130.7, RSMo); Amazon Data Services, Google, and Evergy intervened and signed the stipulation. The order issued November 24, 2025 and took effect December 4, 2025.

rate_cases.next_milestone: Xcel must file a separate clean energy and capacity tariff for very large customers by December 1, 2026
rate_cases.summary: The Minnesota PUC approved Xcel Energy's large-load tariff for customers of 100 MW or more: 15-year minimum contracts, an 80% demand-charge obligation on early exit, and a new dedicated rate class so data-center costs are assigned transparently in future rate cases. The Commission also directed Xcel to file a separate clean energy and capacity tariff by December 1, 2026. Minnesota Power and Otter Tail Power have filed similar proposals.

rate_cases.title: Duke rate-case settlement — expedited large-load tariff track
rate_cases.next_milestone: A Second Amended Comprehensive Revenue Requirement Agreement and Stipulation of Settlement — joined by Duke Energy Carolinas, NCUC Public Staff, industrial/customer groups, and Microsoft Corporation — was filed July 17, 2026 and amended July 20, 2026, committing Duke and Public Staff to submit the special large-load tariff by the end of September 2026. A final NCUC order on the settlement is expected in fall 2026, with new rates beginning January 1, 2027 if approved. On September 14, 2026 Attorney General Jeff Jackson, who declined to sign the settlement, filed a proposal in Duke's rate-case dockets for a new rate class for data centers and other large-load customers (NCDOJ). As of September 22, 2026 no NCUC order on the settlement had been located; the end-of-September large-load tariff submission remains the next dated step.
rate_cases.summary: Duke Energy's proposed 2026 rate-case settlement commits it to an expedited proceeding to establish a formal Large Load Tariff before new rates take effect. Governor Josh Stein and Attorney General Jeff Jackson are pressing Duke — a Ratepayer Protection Pledge signatory — to make the federal pledge binding: "Now, Duke Energy must make that voluntary pledge real. The North Carolina Utilities Commission and Duke Energy must create a legally binding large-load tariff to charge data centers their full freight" (Stein). Duke's spokesperson responds that "data centers and other large-load customers must pay the costs required to serve them while creating long-term value for existing customers."

rate_cases.title: Large-load interconnection rulemaking (DOE-directed ANOPR)
rate_cases.next_milestone: FERC's six Section 206 show-cause orders of June 18, 2026 (PJM's is Docket EL26-67-000) gave each RTO/ISO 60 days — to August 17, 2026 — to justify or reform its large-load interconnection rules, with interventions due July 9, 2026 and comments on the responses due 30 days after they were filed. PJM and the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners moved on July 28, 2026 to hold EL26-67 in abeyance for 90 days (Federal Register notice of Aug. 4, 2026; answers were due Aug. 7). PJM told stakeholders on July 30 that, if the abeyance is granted, it targets a Section 205 filing responding to the show-cause order by early/mid-November 2026. FERC has not announced a date for orders on the show-cause responses.
rate_cases.summary: On October 23, 2025 the Secretary of Energy directed FERC to consider reforms for interconnecting large loads (generally over 20 MW) to the interstate transmission system. On April 16, 2026 FERC committed to act by June 2026, citing its December 2025 PJM co-located-load order, approval of SPP's High Impact Large Load protocols, and the President's Ratepayer Protection Pledge among recent developments; in June 2026 it directed grid operators to reform large-load interconnection procedures, with compliance work ongoing.

rate_cases.title: PJM co-located load rules (data centers at power plants)
rate_cases.next_milestone: PJM's 60-day compliance filing on the June 18, 2026 order was due in mid-August 2026; PJM moved to extend the time for part of it and told stakeholders on July 30, 2026 that it would submit a partial compliance filing, hold stakeholder sessions on July 30, Aug. 18 and Sept. 16, 2026, and — if FERC grants its motions — file the remaining co-located-load compliance around early/mid-November 2026 alongside its large-load Section 205 filing. FERC's review of the May 18, 2026 compliance filing (ER26-1088-001) and of the June 18 order's compliance directives is the next Commission action; no date announced.
rate_cases.summary: In December 2025 FERC found PJM's tariff unjust and unreasonable for lacking clear rules on co-located load — data centers sited at generators — and ordered transparent rules, the question first raised by the rejected Talen/Amazon Susquehanna amended ISA. In April 2026 FERC partially accepted PJM's compliance filing, keeping interconnection-pathway clarity while rejecting PJM's attempt to redefine 'Co-Located Load' and to alter behind-the-meter application requirements. On June 18, 2026 FERC issued its order on rehearing, clarification, compliance and the paper hearing (195 FERC ¶ 61,209; Docket Nos. EL25-49-002 et al.), setting rates and terms for the new Interim NITS, Firm Contract Demand and Non-Firm Contract Demand services (NITS-based rates, a 50 MW behind-the-meter netting threshold applied to load rather than generator nameplate, a curtailment hierarchy and operational penalties) and directing a further compliance filing within 60 days.

rate_cases.title: PA PUC review of emergency load-control rules and large-load cost allocation
rate_cases.next_milestone: Law Bureau and Bureau of Technical Utility Services to present a Tentative Order updating emergency electric load control regulations at the October 1, 2026 public meeting; a technical conference on cost responsibility for large computational loads in fall 2026; final order targeted for the January 28, 2027 public meeting
rate_cases.summary: At its September 10, 2026 public meeting the PUC voted 5-0 on Vice Chair Kimberly Barrow's motion directing staff to draft updates to Pennsylvania's emergency electric load control regulations — including 'greater clarity regarding the order, criteria and circumstances under which customers may be curtailed during pre-emergency and emergency conditions' — and to convene a technical conference examining how costs associated with large computational loads, including data centers, are identified and allocated and their potential impact on non-contributing customers. Barrow: 'The combination of rapid load growth and tightening resource adequacy conditions requires us to carefully examine whether our existing regulatory framework is sufficient for the challenges ahead.' A companion docket (M-2026-3064953) created a Ratemaking Working Group on return on equity, settlement transparency and DSIC returns. This sits alongside the PUC's April 2026 Large Load Tariff Framework (M-2025-3054271, tracked as pa-puc-large-load-model-tariff).

rate_cases.title: I&M base-rate reduction enabled by large-load (data center) growth
rate_cases.next_milestone: IURC decision anticipated in June 2027, with new rates taking effect in late spring / early summer 2027
rate_cases.summary: Indiana Michigan Power filed a base rate case with the IURC on Wednesday, August 26, 2026 asking to reduce Indiana base rates — about 5% on the base-rate line, roughly $59 million in bill reductions in 2027 and about $100 a year for a residential customer using 1,000 kWh a month — and to freeze all rates on Indiana residential bills for three consecutive years, with the reduction attributed to 'load growth and increased revenue from large customers, including data centers.' I&M's Stephanny Smith on the large-load terms that make this possible: 'They pay for 100% of what they use and up to 80 percent of what they say they're going to need, even if they don't use the full amount.' The IURC lists the case as pending base rate case 46454; a decision is expected in June 2027.

rate_cases.title: PPL Electric Utilities base rate case — settlement with large-load (data center) tariff provisions
rate_cases.summary: On June 4, 2026 the PUC voted 5-0 (with partial dissents from Vice Chair Kim Barrow and Commissioners John F. Coleman and Ralph Yanora) to modify and approve a Joint Petition for Settlement resolving PPL Electric's base rate proceeding, reducing the company's annual revenue increase to approximately $275 million from the $356.3 million originally requested. The Commission's release states the settlement includes 'new tariff provisions applicable to certain large-load customers, such as data centers and other high-demand facilities,' including long-term service commitments, minimum demand guarantees and financial protections intended to reduce risk to other customers; PPL Electric was directed to file a compliance tariff for service rendered on and after July 1, 2026. Utility Dive reported that under the settlement filed March 13, 2026 the large-load tariff applies to customers with peak demand of 50 MW or greater at a single facility, or 75 MW or greater in aggregate among facilities taking service at or above 69 kV within a 10-mile radius, with service agreements carrying an initial term of not less than 10 years, a load-ramp schedule of up to five years, minimum load guarantees and exit fees.
